hints.content:
Madalena is trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the volume, in liters, per $1$ fish.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{volume}}}{\maroonD{\text{fish}}} = \purpleD{\text{volume per fish}}$

If we write each unit rate as a decimal, we can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

Let's see what Madalena did instead.

###Finding the unit rates

Tank| $\blueE{\text{Volume (L)}}$ || $\maroonD{\text{Fish}}$ || $\purpleD{\text{Volume per fish}}$
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
$A$  |$40$|$\div$ | $5$|$=$|$8$
$B$|$100$ |$\div$ |$12$ | $\approx$|$8.33$
$C$ |$180$ |$\div$ | $23$|$\approx$| $7.83$

Madalena divided the number of fish by the number of liters instead. That's a different unit rate than she wanted.

###The mistake

Madalena calculated fish per liter instead of liters per fish.

question.content:
Three fish tanks hold different volumes of water and different numbers of fish:

- Tank $A$ holds $40\text{ L}$ and $5$ fish.
- Tank $B$ holds $100\text{ L}$ and $13$ fish.
- Tank $C$ holds $180\text{ L}$ and $23$ fish.

Madalena tried to order the tanks from least to greatest by *volume per fish*, but she made a mistake. Here's her work:

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{5}{40}&=0.125\\\\
\dfrac{13}{100}&=0.13\\\\
\dfrac{23}{180}&\approx 0.127\\\\
\stackrel{\text{Least}}{\underbrace{0.125}_\text{Tank A}} &< \underbrace{0.127}_\text{Tank C} < \stackrel{\text{Greatest}}{\underbrace{0.13}_\text{Tank B}}
\end{align}$

**What was Madalena's mistake?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.content: Madalena calculated fish per liter instead of liters per fish.
Madalena ordered by number of fish instead of by volume per fish.
